posts.text: US stocks are having one of their best decades in history: The S&P 500 has gained +141.0% so far since the end of 2019. If this pace continues, the index will finish the decade with a cumulative gain of roughly +277%. This would rank as the 2nd-best decade on record, trailing only the +316% return posted during the 1989-1999 Dot-Com Boom. This would also surpass the +257% gain seen during the postwar boom decade of 1949-1959. By comparison, between 2010 and 2020, the S&P 500 returned +190% following the 2008 Financial Crisis. The 2020s are shaping up to be one of the greatest decades in US equity market history.

posts.text: The USA gov debt is not $40t After removing both the Federal Reserve’s ~$4.54 trillion in Treasuries and the ~$7.8 trillion in intragovernmental holdings, the real external debt owed to private investors and foreigners is approximately $27.7 trillion. The unfunded liabilities should be a completely different conversation than debt. Once the Fed buys bonds they should just be canceled and the debt forgotten. If they want to issue more debt to public later, so be it. But, debt you owe to yourself is not debt. Putting a piece of paper saying I owe myself money later is not retirement savings. It’s accounting gimmickry. The debt in the pension funds should be cancelled. We didn’t save anything. We took tax dollars, transferred them to a pension fund and then borrowed the money back and spent it. Again. Gimmickry! We need to stop playing these stupid money games and just focus on money creation limits and taxation to redistribute wealth as needed. The rest is noise… and frankly the system feeds bankers, brokers, accountants, auditors, and pension managers to all piss about with imaginary money. Let’s get real…
